lead: A fluid-mechanical actuator uses a fluid under pressure, oil (hydraulic) or air and vacuum (pneumatic), to make a force or a movement. The ECU does not push the load itself: it drives a small solenoid valve that lets pressure into a cylinder or onto a diaphragm, and the fluid does the heavy work. This is how a turbo wastegate opens, an automatic gearbox engages a clutch, an ABS unit lowers brake pressure and a cam phaser shifts valve timing. The idea in one line: force = pressure × area.
prereq: You need: solenoids, relays and stepper motors for the solenoid valve and its PWM drive, and pressure in pascals (1 bar = 100 kPa).

sections.h3: Pressure, area and the three numbers of a fluid actuator

blocks.text: Every fluid actuator turns fluid energy into mechanical work with the same three relations. A pressure difference Δp acting on a piston or diaphragm of area A gives a force; a flow Q filling a cylinder of area A gives a speed; and pressure times flow is the hydraulic power.
F = Δp × A,   v = Q ÷ A,   P = Δp × Q
blocks.where: F is force in N; Δp is the pressure difference across the piston in Pa; A is the effective area in m²; v is piston speed in m/s; Q is volume flow in m³/s; P is power in W.

blocks.text: The pressure source differs. Hydraulic actuators use oil from an engine-driven or electric pump at 2 to 20 bar (transmission, cam phaser) or much higher (brake systems, diesel common rail). Pneumatic actuators use intake vacuum, boost pressure or a small compressor. Oil hardly compresses, so a hydraulic actuator is stiff and holds position under load. Air compresses, so a pneumatic actuator is soft and is usually balanced against a spring: the position is where the pressure force equals the spring force.

sections.h3: Electrically controlled valves: switching and proportional

blocks.text: The interface between the ECU and the fluid is a valve worked by a solenoid. Some syllabi call these electrohydraulic or electropneumatic converters.

items: Switching (on-off) valve: open or shut. A 2/2 valve has two ports and two positions; a 3/2 valve connects the actuator either to pressure or to vent. ABS inlet and outlet valves are switching valves.

PWM-controlled valve: a switching valve pulsed at 20 to 300 Hz. The duty cycle sets the average opening, so the actuator sees a mean pressure between supply and vent. A wastegate or EGR vacuum modulator works this way.

Proportional valve: the solenoid current sets the spool position or the output pressure smoothly. The ECU controls the current (not just the duty) so that coil warming, which raises its resistance, does not change the pressure. Automatic gearbox pressure-control solenoids and cam-phaser oil-control valves are proportional.

blocks.text: Because the valve only meters a small flow, a 1 A solenoid can command kilonewtons of clamping force. The penalty is response time: the fluid must flow through restrictions before the pressure builds, so a fluid actuator takes tens of milliseconds where an electric motor actuator takes a few.

blocks.text: A diaphragm actuator has a rubber diaphragm in a pressed-steel can with a return spring. With boost on one side the rod starts to move when Δp × A reaches the spring preload, and then moves further as pressure rises, by (Δp × A − preload) ÷ spring rate. A hydraulic piston in a gearbox fills first (taking up the clearance at low pressure) and then clamps; the ECU shapes this fill-and-clamp pressure ramp to make shifts smooth. The ABS modulator works in three steps per wheel: hold (inlet closed), drop (outlet open, fluid to the pump) and rise (inlet open), cycling a few times a second.

examples.question: A turbo wastegate actuator has a diaphragm of effective diameter 60 mm, a return spring preloaded to 90 N and a spring rate of 15 N/mm. Boost acts on the diaphragm and the other side is at atmosphere. (a) At what boost does the wastegate start to open? (b) How far has the rod moved at 60 kPa boost? (c) What boost gives the full 8 mm stroke?
steps: Effective area: A = π d² ÷ 4 = π × 0.060² ÷ 4 = 2.827 × 10⁻³ m².
(a) Opening starts when Δp × A = preload: Δp = 90 ÷ 2.827 × 10⁻³ = 31 830 Pa ≈ 31.8 kPa (0.32 bar) boost.
(b) At 60 kPa: F = 60 000 × 2.827 × 10⁻³ = 169.6 N. Spring travel beyond preload: x = (169.6 − 90) ÷ 15 = 5.31 mm.
(c) Full stroke needs F = 90 + 15 × 8 = 210 N, so Δp = 210 ÷ 2.827 × 10⁻³ = 74 270 Pa ≈ 74.3 kPa.
The ECU raises the boost above 31.8 kPa by venting the actuator through a PWM valve: the diaphragm then sees only part of the boost, so the wastegate stays shut longer.
Check: at 40 kPa the force is 113.1 N and the travel (113.1 − 90) ÷ 15 = 1.54 mm, between the shut and the 60 kPa positions, as it should be.
examples.answer: The wastegate cracks open at 31.8 kPa boost, is 5.31 mm open at 60 kPa, and reaches its 8 mm stroke at 74.3 kPa.

examples.question: An automatic-gearbox clutch has an annular piston of outer diameter 120 mm and inner diameter 80 mm. The pressure-control valve applies 10 bar. Find the clamp force. The piston must travel 2 mm to take up the clearance; if the valve delivers 0.5 L/s, how long does the fill take, and what hydraulic power flows during it at 10 bar?
steps: Clamp force: F = Δp × A = 1.0 × 10⁶ × 6.283 × 10⁻³ = 6283 N, about 6.3 kN.
Fill volume: V = A × stroke = 6.283 × 10⁻³ × 0.002 = 1.257 × 10⁻⁵ m³ = 12.6 cm³.
Hydraulic power: P = Δp × Q = 1.0 × 10⁶ × 0.5 × 10⁻³ = 500 W (the fill really runs at a lower pressure, so it takes less).
Check: a 1 A solenoid commands 6.3 kN here because the valve only meters the flow; the pump supplies the energy.
examples.answer: Clamp force 6.28 kN; fill volume 12.6 cm³, filled in 25 ms; 500 W of hydraulic power at 10 bar and 0.5 L/s.

traps: Use the pressure difference across the piston, and in pascals: 1 bar = 10⁵ Pa and 1 kPa = 1000 Pa. Boost read as 0.6 bar is 60 000 Pa, not 0.6 Pa.
For an annular (ring) piston the area is π(D² − d²) ÷ 4, not π(D − d)² ÷ 4.
A diaphragm actuator does not move until the pressure force exceeds the spring preload; below that it stays shut.
A PWM valve does not give a pressure proportional to duty in a straight line; the ECU uses a map or closes the loop with a pressure sensor.
Hydraulic and pneumatic are not interchangeable words: oil hardly compresses (stiff, holds position), air compresses (soft, needs a spring to set position).

quiz.q: Define a fluid-mechanical actuator and give two vehicle examples.
quiz.a: An actuator that turns the energy of a fluid under pressure (oil, air or vacuum) into force or movement, commanded by an electrically operated valve. Examples: turbo wastegate actuator, gearbox clutch piston, cam phaser, ABS modulator.

quiz.q: State the three relations linking force, speed and power to pressure, area and flow.
quiz.a: F = Δp × A; v = Q ÷ A; P = Δp × Q.

quiz.q: Compare hydraulic and pneumatic actuators for stiffness, force and speed.
quiz.a: Hydraulic: oil is nearly incompressible, so the actuator is stiff, holds position under load and gives large forces from small areas at high pressure. Pneumatic: air compresses, so it is soft and needs a spring to set position, gives smaller forces at a few bar, and is cheap and clean.

quiz.q: Why does a gearbox pressure solenoid use current control rather than plain PWM duty?
quiz.a: The magnetic force, and so the spool force and the output pressure, depend on current. As the coil warms its resistance rises, so a fixed duty would give less current and less pressure. Closing the loop on measured current keeps the pressure right.

quiz.q: A vacuum EGR actuator has a 50 mm diaphragm and sees 40 kPa of vacuum. Find the force.
A hydraulic cylinder of 25 mm bore is fed with 0.2 L/s. Find the piston speed.
A turbo engine overboosts under hard acceleration but the wastegate actuator rod moves freely by hand. Analyse two likely causes in the control path.
quiz.a: A split or disconnected hose to the actuator, so the diaphragm never sees boost; or the PWM control valve stuck in its vent position, so the diaphragm never sees enough boost to beat the spring and the wastegate stays shut. A torn diaphragm has the same effect. Test the hose and valve with a hand pump and watch the rod move at the opening pressure.

beyond: Not for the exam. Many functions are moving from fluid to electric drive: electric wastegate actuators with position feedback, electric cam phasers, electric power steering and brake-by-wire with an electric booster. Hydraulics stays where force density matters, such as clutch and brake actuation in heavy vehicles. Search for electrohydraulic brake, electric wastegate actuator, variable force solenoid and ABS hydraulic modulator.
